ceiling_unlocked: What the item unlocks (row 127 asks for the ceiling, not a gain): throughput -- the same contacts in less wall. ROLL-2's slot capacity was 27.3 % empty (8,997 of 32,909 slot-seconds; docs/results/2026-09-27-slurp-throughput-baseline-and-levers.md), reproduced here to the tenth of a second; the first Solver visit alone waited 2.67 s per row on the client. The model-free bench on the locked PLAN cell measured the empty share 15.56 % -> 10.55 % and 2,736 -> 2,899 contacts per hour of contact window (+6.0 %) under the sealed ROLL-2 per-role service times; the honest bound for a flown cell is about +5 % contacts per GPU-hour on a flown cell (the bench's 0.35 s of wall per row against ROLL-2's flown 7.62 s per row), bounded above by lever 1b's +10.1 % for this mechanism; no number is claimed for lever 1a (the flight's 1,055 s of all-slots-empty time is not reproduced on the bench), and the note's +37.6 % lever-1 bound is not approached.

decision_rule_fixed_here: NO-HARM ADMITTED (owner decisions 127 and 159): against the IN-CHAIN A/A arm flown in the same chain, the paired CI95 lower bound of the intent-accuracy delta (primary, decision 133) is not below -0.9943 pp AND the paired CI95 lower bound of the official pooled SLU-F1 delta (the guard) is not below -1.2485 pp -- each metric read at its own Fold A own-null half-width (PLAN vs PLANr, docs/readiness/2026-09-26-slurp-stage3-measurement-instrument-v1.md section 2d). HARMFUL: a measured loss on either metric (CI95 upper bound below zero, decision 25). NEUTRAL-BY-WIDTH IS THE ADMISSION (decision 127). The item is NEVER reported as a gain on either metric. Beside the no-harm read, and as the item's declared ceiling, the THROUGHPUT read: contacts per GPU-hour over each arm's contact window and empty slot-seconds from the server's own per-slot task log joined one-to-one to each arm's sealed trace (scripts/analysis/slotfill_gap_decomposition.py, the note's accounting), arm against A/A. Every verdict carries the per-scenario table in both weightings, the frontier row (decision 75), the delivered-answer agreement rate of arm and A/A, and the request-byte comparison of step 2.
development_numbers_only: Every number this family will produce is a TRAIN Fold A construction-fold development number (owner decisions 28 and 86) and is never a test claim.
failure_policy: Stop and preserve on the first failure. AT MOST ONE root-diagnosed recovery re-registration; a second failure closes the cell and the fix is proven on a four-row dry run. The budget is run-cumulative across attempts.

byte_identity.normalisation: exactly two facts are assigned by ARRIVAL and already differ between two runs of today's dispatcher: the request-id counter (flight-<n>) and the slot number (id_slot on the wire, slot_id / slot_ids in the sealed waves); each flight-<n> and each request sha256 is renamed to its own (row, contact) identity, the slot keys are masked, the runtime-trace digest (computed over the slot ids) is masked while its preimage records are compared, and latency_seconds is dropped. Every other byte is compared.

throughput_estimate.service_model: each request holds its slot for a deterministic draw from the sealed ROLL-2 per-role server busy times (launch to release) of the same role
throughput_estimate.statement: On the proof bench (the locked PLAN cell, 60 rows, 285 contacts per run, each request holding its slot for a draw from ROLL-2's own per-role server busy times) the key moved the empty-slot share 15.6 % -> 10.5 % and contacts per hour of contact window 2,736 -> 2,899 (+6.0 %; the two key-on runs +7.3 % and +4.6 %, the two key-off runs within 0.3 %; the sealed pair +6.1 %), removing 1.40 slot-seconds of empty slot and 0.35 s of wall per row; recall_prefetch alone +6.4 %, role_input_offload alone +2.1 %, gc_freeze alone +1.0 %.
